_what: How computer/hear-a-link.mjs (tool:hear-a-link) turns a link to a video or a recording into its words on the person's Mac. The link readers are `hear-fetcher` rows (records/hear-fetcher-records.json, read through src/data-rows.mjs), tried in order, like computer-sources.json `hearing` rows: the first whose `check` answers here (its program found in `search_path`, then PATH) is the one used. Each fetcher has `info` (prints the page's facts as JSON), `captions` (writes the captions the page offers, in `languages`, into {folder}) and `sound` (writes the sound alone into {folder}); every value in braces is filled when it runs ({url}, {folder}, {languages}, {node}: the node program running this, which some pages need to be read). `languages` are the caption languages asked for when the AI names none. Captions win when the page has them; otherwise the sound is heard with the Mac's first `hearing` row (computer-sources.json). `keep_sound` keeps that sound in the person's files (`folder`, named by the page's title) with its words on it, so it is found by search and never fetched again. `most_minutes` is the longest the fetch may take. Every word the AI reads is under `words`; a link with no words is always answered with why.

confine._what: When enabled, the link reader (a program that fetches a page from the internet) runs confined by computer/confined-run.mjs under this tier: it can write only in its working folder. Off until switched on.

words.needs_url: Send the link to a video or a recording as url.
words.no_fetcher: This Mac has no program that reads video links (such as yt-dlp), so the words could not be read from {url}.
words.no_hearing: {url} has no captions, and this Mac has no program that hears speech (such as mlx-whisper), so its sound could not be turned into words.
words.fetch_failed: Could not read {url} on this Mac: {error}
words.stale_fetcher: Could not read {url} on this Mac: {error}. The page refused this Mac's copy of {fetcher}; updating it often fixes this ({hint}).
words.no_words: {url} was read and heard whole on this Mac, but nobody speaks in it, so it has no words.
words.captions_by: captions on the page, read on this Mac
